jobs.title: Technical Project Manager (Embedded)
jobs.description:
Silicon Quantum Computing (SQC) is at the forefront of global efforts to build the world’s first commercial-scale quantum computer, while delivering quantum-enhanced AI and simulation products to customers today.

Backed by over 25 years of technological excellence, SQC is a full-stack quantum computing company that leverages its proprietary manufacturing process to engineer atomic qubits in silicon with 0.13 nanometer precision. It is the most precise semiconductor manufacturing in the world, enabling systems with world-leading algorithmic fidelity, and a decisive advantage in the global quantum computing race.

Our products are commercially deployed and generating revenue. Watermelon, our quantum-enhanced AI system, is delivering superior results on real-world problems across energy, telecom and finance. Quantum Twins, our simulation platform, provides unparalleled ability to model quantum systems, accelerating molecule and materials discovery.

This is SQC: building the future of computing while delivering quantum impact today.

About The Role

SQC builds gate-based quantum computers in silicon. Our largest programs are multi-year commitments to US government sponsors, delivered against fixed benchmarks, milestones and independent evaluation. We are hiring a Technical Project Manager (Embedded) into Projects to own the hardware and software delivery schedule for the USQC program.

You will own the detailed schedule end to end for the embedded hardware and software work.You will hold a critical path that runs through fabrication, cryogenic test, firmware and software release, and external partner deliverables. Predictability is the core of the job. You will flag early when a tapeout or release is at risk, and when a test result or blocker lands, you will replan quickly and make the consequences clear to the people who need to act on them.

You will work directly with the hardware and software engineering leads on technical readiness, including test plans, release criteria and the hand-off between design, fabrication and integration. You will also manage the embedded partners and subcontractors whose deliverables feed the tapeout and software schedules.

You will report to the Senior Technical Program Manager. Escalate commercial priorities, scope changes and government requirements to them rather than absorbing them into the embedded plan.

Based at our Sydney facility, you will work across the hardware and software teams, moving between technical detail with engineers, clear synthesis for management, and concise updates for the executive and the CEO. This is a role for someone with a genuine project management mindset: structured, disciplined about following defined processes, personally committed to milestones, and comfortable challenging engineering estimates and pushing back when delivery slips.

Role Responsibilities

Own the schedule for cryogenic and conventional ASIC tapeouts, from design freeze through fabrication, characterisation, and foundry coordination.
Own the delivery schedule for compiler, decoder and real-time control plane software releases, including the release train and the R&D deliverables that depend on them.
Build and maintain a credible critical path across hardware, firmware and software, through fabrication, measurement and subcontractor deliverables.
Flag tapeout, foundry, and release risks early, then drive replanning and communicate schedule, cost, and technical impacts.
Plan and track FPGA hardware development, from requirements through deployment.
Plan and track cryogenic interface and control system development, including coordination with external technology partners.
Define test readiness and release criteria with the hardware and software leads and track them to closure.
Run structured risk assessment for each embedded workstream, with a mitigation plan for every dependency.
Hold engineering teams to their commitments, challenge estimates, and escalate slippage to the Senior Technical Program Manager.
Apply SDLC and quality processes consistently across the embedded teams.
Communicate with engineers in technical detail, and with management in concise summaries.

Your Experience

Experience with embedded systems, including FPGA development.
Experience with software release management or SDLC, ideally on compiler, firmware or FPGA workstreams.
A track record of delivering hardware or embedded programs against fixed external milestones, where the deadline does not move.
Experience owning detailed schedules across hardware and software workstreams, including external partners and subcontractors.
Experience managing external partners or suppliers delivering into a hardware program.
A background in semiconductor, test engineering, embedded systems or hardware program management, where hardware dependencies carry real schedule risk.
A structured approach to risk, identifying dependencies early and maintaining credible mitigation plans.
Experience with Agile delivery (Scrum or Kanban) across hardware and software teams.
Willing to hold the line, challenging estimates and pushing back when delivery slips.
Strong communication across engineers and management in a matrix environment.
Comfortable operating to defined processes and formal quality requirements.
A fast learner, comfortable picking up quantum and cryogenic vocabulary on the job. Experience on government-funded programs is desirable.

Equal opportunity

SQC is an equal opportunity employer. We value diverse perspectives and experiences, and encourage applications from candidates who may not meet every listed requirement. If you’re excited about the role and believe you can contribute, we encourage you to apply.

Export controls

This position may require access to export-controlled information or technology. Employment may be subject to applicable export control laws and may require eligibility assessment based on factors such as nationality, citizenship, or residency, and, where necessary, obtaining relevant export licenses or approvals.

About SQC

SQC was founded by renowned physicist and materials scientist Michelle Simmons, who pioneered the field of atomic electronics, including the development of the world’s first single-atom transistor and the first integrated circuit built with atomic precision. Our Chair, Simon Segars, former CEO of Arm, is a leader in the semiconductor industry and was instrumental in developing the processors that powered the mobile computing revolution.

As a full-stack company with in-house QPU manufacturing, SQC can design, produce and test new quantum chips in under a week, enabling rapid iteration and a decisive advantage in the race to build the world’s first commercial-scale quantum computer.

SQC is a high-accountability environment built on a simple principle: Every Atom Counts. If you’re looking to play a meaningful role in building the next frontier of computing, we’d love to hear from you.

Job Description

Research Data Analyst

The Fiscal Policy Initiative and the State & Local Governance Initiative at the Hoover Institution at Stanford University seek multiple predoctoral Research Data Analysts to join our team of policy-oriented academic researchers. The Hoover Institution is a preeminent center of public policy research located at Stanford University. Its fellows are focused on scholarship grounded in the ideals of peace, individual liberty, free enterprise, and limited government.

Current hiring addresses both near-term and future (Summer 2027) needs with flexibility regarding the starting date. Applications will be considered on a rolling basis starting on December 1.

Job Purpose

We invite you to join us to help improve federal, state, and local policymaking. The Fiscal Policy Initiative and the State & Local Governance Initiative, led by Senior Fellow Joshua Rauh , provide credible and actionable academic-quality analyses to inform lawmakers and the public.

Our team currently has particular interest in the recent proposals for state and national wealth taxes and high-income surtaxes. We also anticipate the need to conduct budget scoring of legislative proposals. However, we also welcome applications from candidates with general expertise in our other topic areas.

The primary topic areas of the Fiscal Policy Initiative include federal and state tax policy, entitlement reform, government finances, budget process reform, and the macroeconomic risk of rising federal borrowing.

The primary topic areas of the State & Local Governance Initiative include public finance (in particular, tax policy and public pensions), economic development (regulations, workforce training, and incentive programs), infrastructure (physical and social), and energy and electricity markets.

Our research production model is based on access to unique or restricted datasets, often obtained through data-sharing partnerships with state and local government agencies. These partnerships enable access to administrative data that are not publicly available and allow novel research that produces rigorous, evidence-based policy recommendations. This model leads to high-quality journal publications and ensures that the evidence-based policy recommendations are as accurate as feasible.

The position requires substantial independent work gathering data, building and cleaning datasets, conducting econometric analysis, writing literature reviews, and drafting research results. The position requires the ability to quickly develop new skills in a fast-paced research environment.

The successful candidate for this role will be able to manage and analyze large amounts of information, typically technical or scientific in nature, under the direction of project researchers, investigators, or managers. They will also need to present findings in organized, professional documents. The ability to multitask and appropriately prioritize different projects is essential.

This position is intended to assist the hired candidate to gain research skills and experience ahead of their eventual application to PhD programs. We take pride in preparing our research analysts for a successful career and provide resources and learning opportunities for their professional growth. See our PhD placements here.

The position is intended to be an onsite role at Stanford University or at Hoover’s Washington, D.C. office.

To Apply, Please Submit

A curriculum vitae or resume
A cover letter that describes your fitness for the role
Contact information for at least two references (name, title, email)
College degree transcripts
A research or writing sample that showcases your academic or policy-relevant research skills
A brief statement (500 words) on your research interests in federal, state, and local policy, what attracts you to the Hoover Institution, and examples of scholars or research that has influenced your thinking

Completed Applications Must Be Submitted Online

TERM: One year, renewable; Typical role involves a two-year tenure

Collect data from a variety of sources, including proprietary, surveys, and government records
Manage and clean datasets
Generate research insights using new and existing tools to interpret, analyze, and visualize multivariate relationships and trends in data
Create databases and reports, develop algorithms and statistical models, and perform statistical analyses appropriate to data and reporting requirements
Use system reports and analyses to identify potentially problematic data, make corrections, and suggest solutions
Conduct literature reviews and develop written summaries and reports
Prepare charts, graphs and tables for use by senior researchers and fellows, and for publication and presentation
Analyze data processes in documentation
Collaborate with faculty and research staff on data collection and analysis methods
Provide documentation based on audit and reporting criteria to investigators and research staff
Communicate with government officials, agencies, and industry representatives

Relevant experience may include
: Research assistance for a professor of economics, finance, or statistics; research assistance for a think tank or similar policy research organization; analyst position or substantive internship in economic or financial consulting; analyst position or substantive internship in a government agency such as a central bank, tax authority or treasury/finance department.

Desired/Preferred Knowledge, Skills And Abilities

An understanding of domestic economic policy – particularly in the research areas mentioned earlier - and the effects of these policies on economic activity
Experience with various forms of quantitative analysis
Experience with creating and cleaning databases
Experience with Stata, Python, or R
Programming proficiency and experience in other programming languages such as Matlab, SAS, or C
Experience with data visualization tools, such as Tableau, to present large volumes of data in a user-friendly and visually pleasing format
Experience utilizing common academic software, such as LaTeX/Overleaf
Experience with web-scraping and building websites to convey research results
Effective communication skills and comfort working with prominent individuals.

The Hoover Institution is a preeminent center of public policy research located at Stanford University. Its fellows conduct advanced research regarding economics, politics, history, and political economy—both domestic and foreign—as well as international affairs. Their scholarship is grounded in the ideals of peace, individual liberty, free enterprise, and limited government.

Founded in 1919 by Herbert Hoover before he became the thirty-first president of the United States, the Institution began as a repository of historical material gathered at the end of World War I. The library and archives have grown to be among the largest private repositories of documents on twentieth-century political and economic history. Over time the Institution expanded its mission from collecting archival material to conducting advanced research on contemporary history and economics and applying this scholarship to current public policy challenges. .

Communicate with government officials, grant agencies and industry representatives.

Silicon Quantum Computing (SQC) is at the forefront of global efforts to build the world’s first commercial-scale quantum computer, while delivering quantum-enhanced AI and simulation products to customers today.

Backed by over 25 years of technological excellence, SQC is a full-stack quantum computing company that leverages its proprietary manufacturing process to engineer atomic qubits in silicon with 0.13 nanometer precision. It is the most precise semiconductor manufacturing in the world, enabling systems with world-leading algorithmic fidelity, and a decisive advantage in the global quantum computing race.

Our products are commercially deployed and generating revenue. Watermelon, our quantum-enhanced AI system, is delivering superior results on real-world problems across energy, telecom and finance. Quantum Twins, our simulation platform, provides unparalleled ability to model quantum systems, accelerating molecule and materials discovery.

This is SQC: building the future of computing while delivering quantum impact today.

About The Role

SQC builds gate-based quantum computers in silicon. Our largest programs are multi-year commitments to US government sponsors, delivered against fixed benchmarks, milestones and independent evaluation. We are hiring a Technical Project Manager (Embedded) into Projects to own the hardware and software delivery schedule for the USQC program.

You will own the detailed schedule end to end for the embedded hardware and software work.You will hold a critical path that runs through fabrication, cryogenic test, firmware and software release, and external partner deliverables. Predictability is the core of the job. You will flag early when a tapeout or release is at risk, and when a test result or blocker lands, you will replan quickly and make the consequences clear to the people who need to act on them.

You will work directly with the hardware and software engineering leads on technical readiness, including test plans, release criteria and the hand-off between design, fabrication and integration. You will also manage the embedded partners and subcontractors whose deliverables feed the tapeout and software schedules.

You will report to the Senior Technical Program Manager. Escalate commercial priorities, scope changes and government requirements to them rather than absorbing them into the embedded plan.

Based at our Sydney facility, you will work across the hardware and software teams, moving between technical detail with engineers, clear synthesis for management, and concise updates for the executive and the CEO. This is a role for someone with a genuine project management mindset: structured, disciplined about following defined processes, personally committed to milestones, and comfortable challenging engineering estimates and pushing back when delivery slips.

Role Responsibilities

Own the schedule for cryogenic and conventional ASIC tapeouts, from design freeze through fabrication, characterisation, and foundry coordination.
Own the delivery schedule for compiler, decoder and real-time control plane software releases, including the release train and the R&D deliverables that depend on them.
Build and maintain a credible critical path across hardware, firmware and software, through fabrication, measurement and subcontractor deliverables.
Flag tapeout, foundry, and release risks early, then drive replanning and communicate schedule, cost, and technical impacts.
Plan and track FPGA hardware development, from requirements through deployment.
Plan and track cryogenic interface and control system development, including coordination with external technology partners.
Define test readiness and release criteria with the hardware and software leads and track them to closure.
Run structured risk assessment for each embedded workstream, with a mitigation plan for every dependency.
Hold engineering teams to their commitments, challenge estimates, and escalate slippage to the Senior Technical Program Manager.
Apply SDLC and quality processes consistently across the embedded teams.
Communicate with engineers in technical detail, and with management in concise summaries.

Your Experience

Experience with embedded systems, including FPGA development.
Experience with software release management or SDLC, ideally on compiler, firmware or FPGA workstreams.
A track record of delivering hardware or embedded programs against fixed external milestones, where the deadline does not move.
Experience owning detailed schedules across hardware and software workstreams, including external partners and subcontractors.
Experience managing external partners or suppliers delivering into a hardware program.
A background in semiconductor, test engineering, embedded systems or hardware program management, where hardware dependencies carry real schedule risk.
A structured approach to risk, identifying dependencies early and maintaining credible mitigation plans.
Experience with Agile delivery (Scrum or Kanban) across hardware and software teams.
Willing to hold the line, challenging estimates and pushing back when delivery slips.
Strong communication across engineers and management in a matrix environment.
Comfortable operating to defined processes and formal quality requirements.
A fast learner, comfortable picking up quantum and cryogenic vocabulary on the job. Experience on government-funded programs is desirable.

Equal opportunity

SQC is an equal opportunity employer. We value diverse perspectives and experiences, and encourage applications from candidates who may not meet every listed requirement. If you’re excited about the role and believe you can contribute, we encourage you to apply.

Export controls

This position may require access to export-controlled information or technology. Employment may be subject to applicable export control laws and may require eligibility assessment based on factors such as nationality, citizenship, or residency, and, where necessary, obtaining relevant export licenses or approvals.

About SQC

SQC was founded by renowned physicist and materials scientist Michelle Simmons, who pioneered the field of atomic electronics, including the development of the world’s first single-atom transistor and the first integrated circuit built with atomic precision. Our Chair, Simon Segars, former CEO of Arm, is a leader in the semiconductor industry and was instrumental in developing the processors that powered the mobile computing revolution.

As a full-stack company with in-house QPU manufacturing, SQC can design, produce and test new quantum chips in under a week, enabling rapid iteration and a decisive advantage in the race to build the world’s first commercial-scale quantum computer.

SQC is a high-accountability environment built on a simple principle: Every Atom Counts. If you’re looking to play a meaningful role in building the next frontier of computing, we’d love to hear from you.

Job Description

Research Data Analyst

The Fiscal Policy Initiative and the State & Local Governance Initiative at the Hoover Institution at Stanford University seek multiple predoctoral Research Data Analysts to join our team of policy-oriented academic researchers. The Hoover Institution is a preeminent center of public policy research located at Stanford University. Its fellows are focused on scholarship grounded in the ideals of peace, individual liberty, free enterprise, and limited government.

Current hiring addresses both near-term and future (Summer 2027) needs with flexibility regarding the starting date. Applications will be considered on a rolling basis starting on December 1.

Job Purpose

We invite you to join us to help improve federal, state, and local policymaking. The Fiscal Policy Initiative and the State & Local Governance Initiative, led by Senior Fellow Joshua Rauh , provide credible and actionable academic-quality analyses to inform lawmakers and the public.

Our team currently has particular interest in the recent proposals for state and national wealth taxes and high-income surtaxes. We also anticipate the need to conduct budget scoring of legislative proposals. However, we also welcome applications from candidates with general expertise in our other topic areas.

The primary topic areas of the Fiscal Policy Initiative include federal and state tax policy, entitlement reform, government finances, budget process reform, and the macroeconomic risk of rising federal borrowing.

The primary topic areas of the State & Local Governance Initiative include public finance (in particular, tax policy and public pensions), economic development (regulations, workforce training, and incentive programs), infrastructure (physical and social), and energy and electricity markets.

Our research production model is based on access to unique or restricted datasets, often obtained through data-sharing partnerships with state and local government agencies. These partnerships enable access to administrative data that are not publicly available and allow novel research that produces rigorous, evidence-based policy recommendations. This model leads to high-quality journal publications and ensures that the evidence-based policy recommendations are as accurate as feasible.

The position requires substantial independent work gathering data, building and cleaning datasets, conducting econometric analysis, writing literature reviews, and drafting research results. The position requires the ability to quickly develop new skills in a fast-paced research environment.

The successful candidate for this role will be able to manage and analyze large amounts of information, typically technical or scientific in nature, under the direction of project researchers, investigators, or managers. They will also need to present findings in organized, professional documents. The ability to multitask and appropriately prioritize different projects is essential.

This position is intended to assist the hired candidate to gain research skills and experience ahead of their eventual application to PhD programs. We take pride in preparing our research analysts for a successful career and provide resources and learning opportunities for their professional growth. See our PhD placements here.

The position is intended to be an onsite role at Stanford University or at Hoover’s Washington, D.C. office.

To Apply, Please Submit

A curriculum vitae or resume
A cover letter that describes your fitness for the role
Contact information for at least two references (name, title, email)
College degree transcripts
A research or writing sample that showcases your academic or policy-relevant research skills
A brief statement (500 words) on your research interests in federal, state, and local policy, what attracts you to the Hoover Institution, and examples of scholars or research that has influenced your thinking

Completed Applications Must Be Submitted Online

TERM: One year, renewable; Typical role involves a two-year tenure

Collect data from a variety of sources, including proprietary, surveys, and government records
Manage and clean datasets
Generate research insights using new and existing tools to interpret, analyze, and visualize multivariate relationships and trends in data
Create databases and reports, develop algorithms and statistical models, and perform statistical analyses appropriate to data and reporting requirements
Use system reports and analyses to identify potentially problematic data, make corrections, and suggest solutions
Conduct literature reviews and develop written summaries and reports
Prepare charts, graphs and tables for use by senior researchers and fellows, and for publication and presentation
Analyze data processes in documentation
Collaborate with faculty and research staff on data collection and analysis methods
Provide documentation based on audit and reporting criteria to investigators and research staff
Communicate with government officials, agencies, and industry representatives

Relevant experience may include
: Research assistance for a professor of economics, finance, or statistics; research assistance for a think tank or similar policy research organization; analyst position or substantive internship in economic or financial consulting; analyst position or substantive internship in a government agency such as a central bank, tax authority or treasury/finance department.

Desired/Preferred Knowledge, Skills And Abilities

An understanding of domestic economic policy – particularly in the research areas mentioned earlier - and the effects of these policies on economic activity
Experience with various forms of quantitative analysis
Experience with creating and cleaning databases
Experience with Stata, Python, or R
Programming proficiency and experience in other programming languages such as Matlab, SAS, or C
Experience with data visualization tools, such as Tableau, to present large volumes of data in a user-friendly and visually pleasing format

Experience with web-scraping and building websites to convey research results

About Stanford University’s Hoover Institution

The Hoover Institution is a preeminent center of public policy research located at Stanford University. Its fellows conduct advanced research regarding economics, politics, history, and political economy—both domestic and foreign—as well as international affairs. Their scholarship is grounded in the ideals of peace, individual liberty, free enterprise, and limited government.

Founded in 1919 by Herbert Hoover before he became the thirty-first president of the United States, the Institution began as a repository of historical material gathered at the end of World War I. The library and archives have grown to be among the largest private repositories of documents on twentieth-century political and economic history. Over time the Institution expanded its mission from collecting archival material to conducting advanced research on contemporary history and economics and applying this scholarship to current public policy challenges. .

Minimum Experience
